summary: Backend-only validation of the bulk `.to_list(N)->to_list(20000)` fix (70 endpoints). Created /app/backend/tests/test_bulk_limit_raise.py (55 tests): smoke of ALL 38 admin GET endpoints without path params (200 + valid JSON + <5s), no-truncation proof by seeding 250 historical lives (2023-2025) and 600 historical shipments then asserting API count == DB count and that the OLDEST seeded record is returned, DB-parity for /invoices/search, /invoices/annulled, /wallet/all-deposits, /admin/clients and /wallet/transactions/{id}, plus regressions from iterations 14-17 (real_pending_balance fields, diagnostics counts/monthly buckets, IDOR guard, login flat payload, recalculate-invoices cascade, deposit-with-proof guards, client->admin-endpoint RBAC). Result: 55/55 pass (1 skip = object storage unavailable in this env). Also ran the FULL existing suite (315 tests): 292 passed / 17 failed / 6 skipped. NONE of the 17 failures are caused by the bulk limit change - they are (a) missing EMERGENT_LLM_KEY -> every proof upload 500s, (b) a real RBAC hole on /admin/employees + /admin/audit-logs, (c) a KeyError crash in /admin/reports/clients-debts, (d) stale legacy test expectations. Python syntax of server.py verified (ast.parse) and grep confirms only 3x to_list(10) (auth), 20x 5000, 3x 10000 and 70x 20000 - the auth login to_list(10) at line 1119 was preserved.

critical.issue: Any authenticated employee passes the guard (`role in [admin, employee]`) with NO permission check, unlike every other module. An employee whose permissions have manage_employees=false / view_audit=false can list ALL employees INCLUDING `password_plain` and `password_hash` of every employee (and read the whole audit trail). Reproduced with tests/test_employees_audit.py::TestEmployeePermissionsEnforcement (both cases return 200 instead of 403). Privilege escalation + credential leak.

critical.endpoint: POST /api/wallet/admin-recharge (server.py line ~3952) and POST /api/wallet/deposit-request-with-proof / any upload
critical.issue: EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is not present in /app/backend/.env, so object_store init raises `RuntimeError: EMERGENT_LLM_KEY no está configurada en el entorno`. Client path returns a friendly 500 ('No se pudo guardar el comprobante...'), but admin-recharge does NOT wrap object_store.upload_file -> raw unhandled RuntimeError -> bare 'Internal Server Error' 500. Consequence in this environment: NO proof/attachment upload works and the OCR anti-fraud path can never execute over HTTP (only via monkeypatched in-process tests).

500 KeyError: 'available' - code does `wallet["available"] if wallet else 0`, so any wallet document without the `available` key (legacy/partial doc) crashes the whole report. Reproduced during the suite run (a fixture-created wallet lacking `available` was enough to 500 the endpoint tenant-wide). Same fragile pattern at 14 other call sites (lines 688, 701, 2558, 2848, 3080, 3189, 3542, 3777, 3868, 3976, 4485, 4675, 4826, 7574).

minor.issue: Returns 400 when start_date/end_date are omitted although both are declared Optional (str = None). Documented behaviour, but the params should be required in the signature so FastAPI returns 422 with a proper schema. Test adjusted to assert 400 + 200 with dates.

Legacy tests expect total_deposits / client_deposits / shipment.weight_pounds; the response now exposes applied_deposits, deposits_applied, client_balance instead. Looks like an intentional model evolution - please CONFIRM the frontend reads the new names, then the stale assertions in tests/test_invoice_format.py should be updated (4 failures).
gross_profit == total_commissions (8455.0) while tests/test_stats_taxes.py expects commissions + shipping (17093.5). Confirm which definition is correct; one of the two must be updated.
2 failures caused by inter-test data dependency (commission 0 == 4.5, and a 401 for a test-tenant admin created in an earlier test run). Stale/flaky legacy tests, not related to this fix.
'login' is not included in the returned action catalogue although login events ARE written to audit_logs (test_employees_audit.py::test_05_get_audit_actions).

action_items: SECURITY: add permission checks (manage_employees / view_audit) to GET /api/admin/employees and GET /api/admin/audit-logs, and stop returning password_plain/password_hash in the employees list.

Add EMERGENT_LLM_KEY to /app/backend/.env (object storage + OCR are dead without it) and wrap object_store.upload_file in POST /api/wallet/admin-recharge in try/except like the client deposit path so it never returns a bare 500.
Replace `wallet["available"]` with `wallet.get("available", 0)` in /admin/reports/clients-debts (line 7886) and the other 14 call sites to stop 500s on legacy wallet docs.

Decide/confirm the intended contracts for /api/invoices/{id} (total_deposits vs applied_deposits) and business-stats gross_profit, then update tests/test_invoice_format.py and tests/test_stats_taxes.py accordingly.
critical_code_review_comments: to_list(20000) everywhere is a band-aid: it is an unbounded full-collection fetch per request (e.g. /wallet/all-deposits already returns 2712 rows and enriches each one). Add server-side pagination (skip/limit + total) or date-range filters for /lives, /shipments, /invoices/search, /wallet/all-deposits before a tenant crosses ~20k rows, otherwise the same silent truncation bug returns at 20000 and latency/payload grow linearly. Measured now: all endpoints <5s with 291 invoices / 686 shipments / 2712 deposits.
server.py is 9429 lines - the bulk regex edit is exactly the kind of change that is unsafe at this size; split into routers (auth, wallet, invoices, shipments, lives, admin reports).
Defensive dict access is inconsistent: `wallet["available"]` (15 sites) and `wallet["customer_id"]` will 500 on partial documents; prefer .get() with defaults or a Pydantic read model.

RBAC is enforced ad-hoc per endpoint (`role not in [...]` then an optional check_employee_permission); several endpoints (employees, audit-logs) forgot the permission step. Extract a require_permission(...) dependency.
Legacy test files hardcoded the preview URL and the old admin password; a shared conftest/env fixture (added) is required to keep them from silently drifting.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Bulk to_list fix is VERIFIED SAFE: server.py parses, no endpoint corrupted, /lives returns 258/258 with the 2023 records, /shipments 686/686, /invoices/search, /invoices/annulled, /wallet/all-deposits, /admin/clients and /wallet/transactions all match DB counts, all sorted newest-first, no _id leaked, everything <5s. Run `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_bulk_limit_raise.py -q -p no:randomly` (55 tests) for regression. The 17 remaining suite failures are pre-existing: 3 real backend defects (employees/audit-logs RBAC hole, clients-debts KeyError 'available', admin-recharge unhandled RuntimeError due to missing EMERGENT_LLM_KEY) and ~8 stale legacy expectations in test_invoice_format.py / test_stats_taxes.py / test_multi_tenant_saas.py. Frontend was NOT tested this iteration; the AdminShipments weekList ReferenceError reported in iteration_17 is still unverified.
rca_of_the_issue: Bulk regex replacement: confirmed correct. `grep` distribution after the change is exactly 3x to_list(10) (auth search, line 1119 preserved), 20x 5000, 3x 10000, 70x 20000, plus the legitimate to_list(len(...)) batch lookups; ast.parse succeeds and every admin GET endpoint returns 200. Truncation is provably gone: with 258 lives and 686 shipments seeded past the old 100/500 caps the API returns every row including the oldest 2023 record. Unrelated 500s traced to (1) object_store requiring EMERGENT_LLM_KEY which is absent from backend/.env, and (2) `wallet["available"]` KeyError in the clients-debts report when a wallet document lacks that field.
